unit.title: Position and Direction
unit.blurb: Reading and plotting coordinates in the first quadrant, finding missing vertices of shapes, and translating points and shapes on a grid.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Read and plot coordinates in the first quadrant, including vertices of shapes.

O2.t: Translate points and 2D shapes on coordinate grids and describe translations.

p: **Coordinates** give the position of a point: **(x, y)**. Go **across** the x-axis first, then **up** the y-axis.
The point (0, 0) is called the **origin**. (4, 2) is 4 across and 2 up.

lesson.t: Why the order of coordinates matters
p: (2, 5) and (5, 2) are different points. We agree that the first number is across (x) and the second is up (y).

lesson.q: A square has corners (1, 1), (4, 1) and (4, 4). Find the fourth.

p: (2, 5) and (5, 2) are different points. x comes first.

options.fb: The first number is across (x).
Across comes first, then up.
Correct.

p: A **translation** slides a point or shape without turning or flipping it. Every point moves the same distance in the same direction.
'3 right, 2 up' adds 3 to x and 2 to y: (1, 4) → (4, 6).

lesson.t: Why a translation does not turn a shape
p: In a translation every point moves the same distance in the same direction. The shape slides; it does not turn or flip.

lesson.q: Translate (2, 3) 4 squares right and 1 square down.

p: Move one corner at a time.
Right/left changes x; up/down changes y.
After a translation the shape is the same size and faces the same way.

Before you read on: does a translation change the size of a shape?

options.fb: Correct.
A translation only slides the shape.
It never changes the size.
